name: Turkey

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 85%, Alevi about 10 to 15%

snapshot: Istanbul's jailed mayor, Erdoğan's strongest rival, went on trial with 414 co-defendants while a court ousted the main opposition party's leader.
culture: Turkey bridges Europe and Asia, and Istanbul, once Constantinople, holds Byzantine and Ottoman wonders like the Hagia Sophia. Turkish TV dramas are the world's second most exported after America's. Tea, coffee, kebabs and baklava, the hamam and football rivalries between Galatasaray, Fenerbahçe and Beşiktaş are part of daily life. Kurds make up about a fifth of the population.
society: Turkey is a major manufacturing and tourism economy and hosts the world's largest refugee population, mostly Syrians. High inflation since 2021 hit living standards. The PKK announced its dissolution in 2025 after a 40-year insurgency. Erdoğan's power has grown since a 2016 coup attempt, after which tens of thousands were purged.
situation: In 2019, a little-known district mayor named Ekrem İmamoğlu won Istanbul, Turkey's largest city and economic heart, ending 25 years of rule there by Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's party and its predecessors. Erdoğan himself began his rise as Istanbul's mayor, and once said whoever wins Istanbul wins Turkey. In March 2025, on the day İmamoğlu was nominated as the opposition's presidential candidate, he was arrested. In 2026, the government moved against his party too.

Since March, İmamoğlu has been on trial in a prison courtroom along with 414 co-defendants, accused of running a vast criminal network; he denies it. In May, a court annulled the 2023 congress of his Republican People's Party (CHP), Turkey's oldest party, founded by Atatürk, removing its leader Özgür Özel and reinstating his predecessor (Turkish Minute). Then in July, as Erdoğan hosted NATO's 36 leaders in Ankara, İmamoğlu was ejected from court after asking the judge: "How can you explain to world leaders at the NATO summit, in Turkey, in Ankara, the silencing of Ekrem İmamoğlu?" The European Parliament's rapporteur noted it was "statistically impossible" that three of his hearings fell the same day by chance (AP via ABC News). The summit itself showcased Turkey's value to the West as NATO's second-largest army and a key player in Syria, Ukraine and the Black Sea, which critics say is why Western governments have said little.
power: A presidential republic since a 2017 referendum gave the president sweeping executive powers and abolished the post of prime minister. The president is directly elected for five years; the 600-seat Grand National Assembly makes laws but has limited oversight. Courts are widely seen as under government influence.
holders: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (AKP), in power as prime minister or president since 2003; next election due 2028.
